chunks: And by this chain, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah's blessings be upon him) used to say: 'Indeed We revealed it on the Night of Power'

God Almighty and Majestic spoke the truth. God revealed the Quran on the Night of Power. 'And what will make you know what the Night of Power is?' — the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I do not know.' God Almighty and Majestic said: 'The Night of Power is better than a thousand months' in which there is no Night of Power. He asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family): 'Do you know why it is better than a thousand months?' He said: 'No.' He said: 'Because therein the angels and the Spirit descend by the permission of their Lord for every affair', and when God Almighty and Majestic permits something, He has approved it. 'Peace it is until the break of dawn' — He is saying: 'My angels and My Spirit submit their greetings upon you, O Muhammad, with My greeting, from the beginning of their descent until the break of dawn.'

Then He said in another part of His Book: 'And guard yourselves against a trial which may not afflict particularly those of you who are unjust' (8:25) — regarding 'Indeed We revealed it on the Night of Power' (97:1). And He said in another part of His Book: 'And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; indeed messengers have passed away before him; if then he dies or is killed, will you turn back upon your heels? And whoever turns back upon his heels, he shall not do harm to God in the least, and God will reward the grateful' (3:144).

He is saying in the first verse: when Muhammad passes away, the people of opposition to God's command Almighty and Majestic will say: 'The Night of Power expired with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).' So this is a trial that afflicted them specifically, and by it they turned back upon their heels — because if they were to say 'It did not pass away,' then there would inevitably have to be a command from God Almighty and Majestic during it, and if they acknowledged the command, there could be no escape from there being a Master for it.

key_terms.أَمْر: Command/affair — God's divine command or decree, particularly regarding the governance of creation
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْخِلَافِ: People of opposition — those who opposed the divinely-appointed Imam after the Prophet's death
key_terms.صَاحِب: Master/possessor — here referring to the Imam who holds authority during Laylat al-Qadr
key_terms.فِتْنَة: Trial/tribulation — the spiritual and political strife of denying the Imam's authority
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: Laylat al-Qadr — the Night of Power/Destiny, the blessed night of the first revelation of the Quran

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam Zayn al-Abidin say Laylat al-Qadr proves the necessity of the Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) quotes Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) who explains the exegesis of Surah al-Qadr (97), presenting a theological argument for the continuation of Laylat al-Qadr after the Prophet's death as proof of the necessity of the Imamate. The argument is that those who opposed the Imam were caught in a logical dilemma: if they admitted that Laylat al-Qadr continues, they would have to acknowledge that God's commands must descend to someone with authority — i.e., an Imam — and if they denied its continuation, they would contradict the Quran. The hadith connects Quranic verses from Surah al-Qadr (97), Surah al-Anfal (8:25), and Surah Al Imran (3:144) to establish that the Imamate is a theological necessity grounded in the ongoing nature of divine revelation and governance.
